--- ABSTRACT ---
[OBJECTIVES]: CD100, also known as Sema4D, is a member of the semaphorin family and has important regulatory functions that promote immune cell activation and responses. The role of CD100 expression on B cells in immune regulation during chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains unclear.
[MATERIALS AND METHODS]: We longitudinally investigated the altered expression of CD100, its receptor CD72, and other activation markers CD69 and CD86 on B cells in 20 chronic HCV-infected patients before and after treatment with pegylated interferon-alpha (Peg-IFN-α) and ribavirin (RBV) by flow cytometry.
[RESULTS]: The frequency of CD5+ B cells as well as the expression levels of CD100, CD69 and CD86 was significantly increased in chronic HCV patients and returned to normal in patients with sustained virological response after discontinuation of IFN-α/RBV therapy. Moreover, the increased CD100 expression via IFN-α was inversely correlated with the decline of the HCV-RNA titer during early-phase treatment.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Peripheral B cells show an activated phenotype during chronic HCV infection. Moreover, IFN-α therapy facilitates the reversion of disrupted B cell homeostasis, and up-regulated expression of CD100 may be indirectly related to HCV clearance.

key_findings.finding: Direct evidence exists in PMID 25436996 (PLOS ONE, 2014): 20 patients with chronic HCV were studied longitudinally before/after pegylated IFN-α plus ribavirin. Flow cytometry showed elevated CD100/Sema4D on peripheral B cells (including B-cell subsets) during chronic HCV; IFN-α therapy further up-regulated B-cell CD100 in early virological responders, and in-vitro IFN-α experiments confirmed inducibility. CD100 up-regulation was inversely correlated with early-phase HCV-RNA decline, while markers and CD100 returned toward normal after sustained virological response. This is strong direct clinical association plus pharmacologic/in-vitro support, but the inverse correlation and treatment design do not prove that HCV directly induces CD100 or that CD100 causes viral clearance.

key_findings.finding: PMID 29163508 (Frontiers in Immunology, 2017) provides supportive but non-B-cell evidence: in chronic HCV patients, IFN-α significantly up-regulated CD100 on NK cells, with inverse association to early HCV-RNA levels; coculture with HCV-expressing Huh7.5 cells or IFN-α and Plexin-B1/B2-dependent NK killing supported a functional mechanism. It should not be counted as direct evidence for B-cell CD100 because the measured effector cells were NK cells.
